belief: My role is fixed, and I can't be more than that.
origins: Family, culture, or church may tell us who we are allowed to be: the helper, the provider, the quiet one, the one who never leaves. Dreams are dismissed, abilities overlooked, and we shrink to fit. Eventually we forget what we wanted.
teaches: “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” God’s gifts are given to each person, and Paul says the body has many parts, each needed. “Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.” Deborah was a prophetess who judged Israel, and Lydia led a business. God calls people in many ways. While Christians differ on some roles in marriage and church, nobody has the right to say you cannot grow in the gifts God gave you.
self_statements: This is all I am allowed to be.
I cannot change what is expected of me.
It is too late to be anything else.
I was born for this role only.
People would not accept me in another role.
errors: Believing I am either in my role or out of place.
Assuming others will not accept growth.
Feeling stuck and concluding that I am.
questions: Who assigned my role, and was it God, family, or culture?
What gifts do I have that my role does not use?
What does Scripture say about gifts?
What did I dream of before I learned to shrink?
Where might I grow while remaining faithful to my commitments?
truth: God gave me gifts and calling beyond a label. I can honor my commitments and responsibilities while growing in the gifts He gave. My worth and my potential are not limited by someone else’s script.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
I can think of myself with sober judgment.
My worth is not limited by a script.
log: Each week, note one step of growth.
actions: Write what you once hoped to do.
Try a class, a skill, or a conversation.
Ask a trusted friend or mentor.
prayer: Father, You made me with gifts. Free me from scripts that shrink me. Show me how to grow faithfully and use what You gave me. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “God gave me gifts, and I can grow in them.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “My role is fixed, and I can't be more than that.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
